liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodleloo** (3 reviews): Jerry plays real guitar in the opening Mississippi, unlike in some weaker 1995 performances; Jerry was off the rails within a verse of the opening Half-Step, signaling a loose performance [12][14][15]
- **Attics of My Life** (2 reviews): Attics of My Life and Sugar Magnolia were a relief, though not enough to rescue the show; Reviewer's only live Attics; it seemed out of place but lifted a decent post-drums [8][15]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Reviewer found Bird Song wild and extreme, one of the few high points of an otherwise bad night [6]
- **The Promised Land** (1 review): Promised Land closed the first set; the reviewer disliked it while a nearby fan danced happily [11]
- **Corrina** (1 review): Corrina brought welcome relief during a show the reviewer found weak [8]
- **Mississippi Half Step** (1 review): Reviewer says the band's faster tempos drain the magic from Half Step [13]

## Setlist highlights

- **Dear Mr. Fantasy**: back after 311 archived shows (1474 days) [16]

## The recordings

- **gd94-08-03.fob-schoeps.sisler-pujol.20291.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 19 songs; 180 min; rated 1.5/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd94-08-03.aud.unknown.8728.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 153 min; rated 1.71/5 by 14 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer rates the audience recording quality a B or better [10]
- **gd1994-08-03.fob.schoepsCMC54.travitz-litz.85704.flac1648**: source not stated; 18 songs; 172 min; rated 2.6/5 by 5 [3]

## Around the show

- Listener sat fourth row center and nearly left, until the band moved into Corrina [8]
- Reviewer attended on their birthday and left early, disgusted [9]
- Reviewer's 27th show of a 28-show run covering summer 1994; this was the tour's last venue [10]
- Reviewer attended both Giants Stadium nights; a nearby dancing woman loved the first-set closer while the reviewer found it awful [11]
- Reviewer was in the crowd, where bourbon was passed around in exchange for jokes [14]
- Half of the reviewer's group walked out before Drums, after a weak pre-drums stretch [15]
- Reviewer felt the crescendos matched the energy of the rest of that summer's shows [10]
- Reviewer says 1994 swung up and down; leaving this show, they felt the band was finished [11]
- Compared with some 1995 shows, Bob hits most notes here and Jerry is actually playing guitar [12]
- Reviewer sees this show as a prelude to the rough summer of 1995 [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd94-08-03.fob-schoeps.sisler-pujol.20291.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Dan Sisler; transferred by Marc Pujol; source: Audience: Schoeps MK4's [1]. Also: Recorded from 25th row center with Schoeps cmc5/mk4 mics, Sonosax, Sony D10, then Sony D7 at 44.1; Dan Sisler cloned the master DAT; Marc Pujol converted to seekable SHN via Soundforge and CDwave [1]
- **gd94-08-03.aud.unknown.8728.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience: Unknown Mics [2]
- **gd1994-08-03.fob.schoepsCMC54.travitz-litz.85704.flac1648**: taped by Travitz & Keith Litzenberger; transferred by Watson; source: Schoeps CMC54's>Aerco>Sony TCD-D10PROII, FOB (@15th Row Center) [3]. Also: Watson transferred the front-of-board Schoeps DAT tapes, which had been sitting unused in the uploader's collection [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by D.King Gallery: [Grateful Dead 8/3/1994 NY Giants Stadium Backstage Pass](https://www.dking-gallery.com/store/Dead_Pass_940803.html) [17]
